question.problem:
Given that $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}+4x}{{x}^{2}+3x-4},$ which of the following statements is correct?

I. ${lim}_{x\to (-4)^{-}}f(x)=\infty $

II. ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)=-\infty $

III. ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty $
question.worked_solution:
First, let's factor the numerator and denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}+4x}{{x}^{2}+3x-4} \\  & =\frac{x(x+4)}{(x+4)(x-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain is  $x\ne -4,1,$ and we notice that the function can be simplified:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)=\frac{x}{x-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we see that the function has the only vertical asymptote $x=1.$ So statement I is false.

To find  ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x),$ and  ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x),$ we evaluate $f(x)$ at $x$-values very close to $x=1$ from the left and right.

| $x$ | $0.99$ | $0.999$ | $1$ | $1.001$ | $1.01$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $-99$ | $-999$ | $\text{undefined}$ | $1\,001$ | $101$ |

All values are negative and get smaller and smaller as $x\to 1$ from the left and all values are positive and get larger and larger as $x\to 1$ from the right. Therefore, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty ,\,{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)=\infty 
$$

Consequently, statement II is false and statement III is true.

In conclusion, only statement III is correct. A plot of the function is shown below.
